Nonzero calls 0x82CF78D8(player,unit,r27,r26) at 0x82CDEEA8 and leaves this case. Zero reaches 0x82CDEEB0. The flag's mode name and the earlier helper's effects remain unbound.

zeroModeRoute.queuedState: 0x82CDEEB0..0x82CDEF00 stores target halfwords at U+0x22/+0x24 and-1 at U+0x18; it sets U+0xC bit 0x1 and clears bit 0x40. It also writes float target components at 0x82F771C4/0x82F772D0. Inputs that stay unchanged and normal helper returns are premises.
zeroModeRoute.sdiGuard: 0x82CDEF54..0x82CDF100 checks the center and eight table-derived offsets. Each selected test requires tile halfword bit 0x1, a signed tile-owner byte unequal to actor, and the indexed city's+0x10 bit 0x40000. Qualifying tests replace r20, initially-1, with that city index and set U+0xC bit 0x40. The offset tables, valid coordinate domain and complete tile and city coherence that stays valid are not shown here; do not infer universal range or first-match priority.
zeroModeRoute.presentationStart: 0x82CDF120..12C ORs 0x02200100 into 0x82FFE7C4;0x82CDF134 calls receiver 0x8314F76C virtual+0x1F4 with r4=0 and retains the result. No actual installed target or displayed effect is identified.
zeroModeRoute.wait: 0x82CDF144..180 repeats while 0x82FFE7C4 bit 0x02000000 or 0x82FFE7C0 mask 0x30000 remains set, calling 0x82E2A838. A zero low-byte pump result can also leave the loop. Exit therefore does not prove a completed animation; the later code clears 0x100 and 0x200000 in 0x82FFE7C4.
zeroModeRoute.damageAndConsumption: Only r20==-1 calls 0x82CF7428 at 0x82CDF1A8. Both local outcomes then clear U+0xC bit 0x8000 and call 0x82D02390(player,unit,0) at 0x82CDF1C4. Its mode 0 arm marks U+0xC bit 31 and writes-1 to U+0x26, with accepted linked-unit cleanup. This is a consumption path that applies only after required returns, not proof that every launch reaches it or that damage succeeded.
zeroModeRoute.postOutcome: The no-selected-SDI arm writes 3000 to 0x830E4548 and clears target tile bit 0x20; the constant's time units are not assigned. The selected-SDI arm formats the message at 0x82157518 using the kept city and calls advisor 0x82CE8338 at 0x82CDF268. It does not establish a visible message. Both reach virtual+0xC4 at 0x82CDF27C, with virtual+0x1F0 at 0x82CDF29C called only under a condition on the low byte of the earlier +0x1F4 result.

damageHelper.guard: 0x82CF749C..0x82CF7574 independently scans center and table offsets with coordinate arithmetic and checks a populated tile's actual city owner against actor and city+0x10 bit 0x40000. A qualifying different-owner city calls 0x82D03388 at 0x82CF75CC and returns. Unlike the dispatch scan, this guard reads city owner; no blanket equivalence of the two scans is asserted. The scan is not side-effect-free: its other selected arm clears tile bit 0x10 and calls virtual+0x104 at 0x82CF7560 before continuing.
damageHelper.state: On the remaining path, 0x82CF7654..0x82CF76F0 changes city population byte+3 with center-versus-offset division and a bit 0x1 building exception; further guarded city work and pair-state writes follow. 0x82CF7788..0x82CF7824 scans up to 256 unit records of the selected tile owner, requires byte+0!=0xFF, dead bit 31 clear and matching coordinates, and has an alternating-survivor exception for noncenter city tiles. Qualified records call 0x82D02390(mode 0) at 0x82CF7814. This establishes gameplay-state and kill paths, not a universal kill count or every callee's effects.
damageHelper.finish: The selected tail changes center tile state or calls virtual+0x174, then requests recount 0x82D11AD8 at 0x82CF78AC and increments a player-indexed word. Reaching or returning through this tail is not observed. The local inspected body contains no direct RNG recurrence, but indirect and transitive callees are unexpanded.

nonzeroModePrefix.entry: 0x82CF78D8 preserves actor, unit and target, writes 2 to 0x830E45B8 and float target components, then calls 0x82CFADF0. Its selected prefix also tests city SDI state.
nonzeroModePrefix.effectRequest: The selected no-interception arm calls 0x8314F76C virtual+0x178 at 0x82CF7A50 with kind 2, actor and target, retaining the returned value. It later polls virtual+0x17C at 0x82CF7AD0 and pumps 0x82E2A838. Installed target, token lifetime, actual effect and downstream completion beyond the queried prefix are not confirmed. Do not apply the zero-mode consumption proof to this route.

currentEvidence.method: Serialized foreground read-only canonical Ghidra queries, supported flat-image SHA256 equality, 943 unique native words matched to file bytes, fixed-four-byte Capstone 5.0.7 decoding and corroboration from the recompiled copy of the exact function. Save-thunk truncation was preserved; no canonical repair.
currentEvidence.qualification: Read-only words are static evidence. Mode values, receivers, whether returns, aliases and lifetimes stay valid, the exact save and build, and gameplay and display outcomes need a matched runtime observation. Existing Move observations for non-specialized Moves do not transfer to nuclear actions.

runtimeObservation.required: Record the actor, unit, command, target and mode; compare unit, SDI city, population and victim records before and after; tie the damage and kill calls and the presentation wait exit to the same event and video.

RVA-F-0333.falsification: Different definition mask, mode branch, SDI predicates, damage-call guard, consume arguments or wait exit invalidate the respective static result. Changed live inputs, opaque calls or later state changes can invalidate a runtime interpretation without changing the instructions.
RVA-F-0333.conclusion: A specialized Move branch can consume an ICBM after either selected interception or a damage-helper call that applies only under a condition. Gameplay consumption, gameplay outcome and visible presentation are separate. Missing pixels alone do not demonstrate a missing gameplay effect; a consumed missile alone does not demonstrate successful damage.

RVA-F-0334.reentryGate: Identify the actual nuclear virtual target and effect instance or a first failing draw or resource in a matched event. Tie creation, asset success, update and render, bindings that stay valid, resolve and sample, and destruction to that instance. Do not repeat global string and reference searches without a new discriminator.
guards: Do not equate a crater asset with the missile model or all explosion passes.
Do not set or remove a suppression option from its label alone.
Do not treat an exposure-name handle as the parameter value consumer.
Do not infer that native rendering bypasses or fixes a guest effect-lifetime error.
RVA-F-0334.conclusion: Named nuclear presentation anchors exist, but the gameplay request-to-scene-instance-to-D3D link remains unresolved. These four sites narrow a future trace without assigning the reported flicker or disappearance to particular responsible code.
